answer: Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. Each identity must lock a bond, called an atlas, before it can post or attest. A single pigment checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 334 aliases therefore costs 476 bonds held for 9 days each, plus the marble attestations those aliases can never earn. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
